issues.description: NASM preprocessor define is spelled inconsistently across Makefiles: the example_program Makefile passes the preprocessor define as "-Dera=1" while the tests Makefile passes "-dera=1". These refer to the same conceptual define (era) but are written with different option spellings. Because NASM preprocessor defines are controlled by the -D option, the inconsistent spelling may result in the 'era' symbol being defined in one build invocation and not in the other, causing different conditional assembly paths (inclusion/exclusion of the test/main code and io.inc) and non-reproducible builds.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent NASM -D option spelling in all Makefiles. Replace any occurrences of "-dera=1" with the canonical "-Dera=1" in the tests Makefile(s) (both template and solution) so every NASM invocation defines the same 'era' symbol. Verify all NASM commands across the repository use the same -D form to ensure conditional assembly paths are identical between building the example program and the tests.
